verdicts.evidence: pr72680_tree/products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:1140-1153 (receiver leg's only check = repo-config resolution; no _is_bot_authored, no find_signal_implementation_run, no fork check before stamping inbox_review at 1176-1230) vs tasks.py:169-207 (webhook leg requires bot author, same-repo head, facade linkage match, resolver opt-in); tasks.py:947 (inbox_review bypasses review_mode gate on webhook path); temporal/activities.py:449-451 (self_driving_review set purely from output.inbox_review, comment falsely claims both paths positively link the PR); products/review_hog/backend/receivers.py:93,126-139 (pr_url read straight from TaskRun.output, forwarded to stamphog); receivers.py:34-35 (TaskRun.branch seeded with BASE branch by auto-start); products/tasks/backend/webhooks.py:68-76,184-185,203-212 (branch-matched backstop writes a same-repo PR's URL onto the run when output.pr_url unset, saving with update_fields=["output","updated_at"] which re-fires the receiver)
verdicts.notes: Verified end to end. The receiver leg posts a real head-pinned GitHub approval with self-driving provenance while applying none of the positive-identification checks the sibling webhook leg treats as load-bearing, and it also skips the review_mode/write-permission gates entirely. The trust chain bottoms out in TaskRun.output.pr_url, which the tasks webhook backstop can mis-bind: auto-start seeds TaskRun.branch with the BASE branch, so a same-repo human PR whose head ref equals that base (e.g. a main->release promotion PR) opened before the agent records its own PR gets bound to the signals run and then auto-approved with every human gate bypassed. Fork-safety and write-once upstream narrow but don't close this (the dangerous case is same-repo and pre-pr_url by construction). Reachability needs a multi-condition coincidence, so not must_fix; but the worst case satisfies branch protection with zero human review and the fix (drop out if not _is_bot_authored(pr) after the fetch, ideally re-verify linkage via find_signal_implementation_run) is a cheap mirror of the existing sibling guard, so should_fix rather than consider. The prior triage note's downgrade-to-consider underweights that the base-branch seeding makes the collision a real pattern (promotion PRs from main), not just an exotic name collision.

verdicts.notes: Confirmed as written. A prompt-injected or buggy signals implementation agent (or any task:write caller) can point output.pr_url at any open PR in any repo the team has a synced+enabled Stamphog config for — including a human-authored ready PR — and Stamphog will bypass the bot/draft/review_mode/write-permission gates and post a real head-pinned GitHub approval capable of satisfying required reviews. Prerequisites (synced config, opted-in acting reviewer, one signals run) are the feature's normal operating conditions, and an end-to-end test exercises exactly this chain. Fix is cheap and matches the codebase's own stated invariant: mirror find_signal_implementation_run linkage (require the match's signal_report_id to equal the caller's) or at minimum assert the fetched PR is bot-authored and draft before stamping inbox_review; also correct the false comment at activities.py:448-450.

verdicts.notes: The receiver leg is a new approval-capable entry point with a clear trust-boundary asymmetry versus the webhook leg. A prompt-injected self-driving agent (the exact threat the carve-out gating exists to defend against) can set output.pr_url to another PR in any Stamphog-enabled repo for its team and obtain an unearned Stamphog approval, bypassing the bot-author/draft gates that normally refuse such PRs and satisfying required reviews with zero human in the loop — breaking the PR's own "positively identified carve-out rather than a trigger-side bypass" invariant. Preconditions are elevated (compromised agent + opted-in reviewer + enabled repo), which caps blast radius, but the consequence is a security-control (approval) bypass on a path whose webhook sibling is deliberately hardened, so it clears the security/auth-gap keep bar. Fix: re-attest team_id/task_run_id/signal_report_id/repository/pr_url describe the same non-internal signal implementation run (and mirror the webhook PR-shape checks) before stamping inbox_review; at minimum constrain the parsed repo to task.repository.

verdicts.evidence:
Verified in the frozen worktree (all paths under .../pr75215_tree):

1. The new receiver leg does zero positive identification of the PR. products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:1109-1245 (`process_inbox_pr_review`): parses the URL (L1130), resolves any enabled StamphogRepoConfig for that repo in the team (L1140-1147), fetches the PR (L1159), checks only `state == "open"` (L1166) and a non-empty head sha (L1170), then stamps `output={"inbox_review": {...}}` and creates a QUEUED ReviewRun (L1176-1230). There is no `_is_bot_authored(pr)` call, no `head.repo.full_name == repo_config.repository` fork check, and no `find_signal_implementation_run` PR→run linkage check anywhere in the function.

2. That provenance is the sole unlock for the engine carve-out. products/stamphog/backend/temporal/activities.py:448-451 passes `self_driving_review=bool(output.get("inbox_review"))`, with the comment "it is set exclusively from the run's inbox provenance, which both trigger paths stamp only after positively linking the PR to a signals implementation run" — false for this leg. products/stamphog/AGENTS.md:96-98 repeats the claim ("only the two linkage-verified trigger paths stamp"), and AGENTS.md:110-113 documents that carved-out runs deliberately "bypass the review-mode and author-write-permission gates".

3. The webhook leg does perform exactly the checks the receiver leg omits: tasks.py:169 `_is_bot_authored`, L176-178 head-repo == repo fork check, L189-200 `find_signal_implementation_run` + team recheck; and tasks.py:944 / L966-968 skip `_review_mode_skip_reason` and `_author_lacks_write_permission` when `inbox_review is not None`. So the two legs of the same carve-out are asymmetric, and the receiver leg's run never passes any of those gates (they live in `process_pull_request_event`, not the workflow).

4. `output.pr_url` is caller-writable and unvalidated. products/tasks/backend/facade/api.py:2139-2154 (`set_task_run_output`) writes caller output wholesale through `_apply_caller_output`, which constrains only `_WEBHOOK_ATTESTED_RUN_OUTPUT_KEYS = {"pr_merged"}` (api.py:1770-1788); pr_url is not attested. The PATCH path api.py:2038-2044 carries the same comment ("this PATCH surface is caller-controlled too"). Serializer does no URL validation (presentation/serializers.py:671-674). The endpoint is `runs/<id>/set_output/` with `required_scopes=["task:write"]` (presentation/views/api.py:1101-1121). Only the GitHub backstop writer is fork-safe (products/tasks/backend/webhooks.py:178-185), not the API writers.

5. Reachability by a low-privilege actor: the qualifying task is a signals implementation task, and products/tasks/backend/visibility.py:22-46 puts `Task.OriginProduct.SIGNAL_REPORT` in `TEAM_VISIBLE_ORIGIN_PRODUCTS`, so `task_control_q` grants **any team member** control of it. Writing `output.pr_url` re-fires the receiver (products/review_hog/backend/receivers.py:85-139 only requires update_fields containing "output", non-internal task with signal_report_id, and an opted-in assigned reviewer) → `queue_inbox_pr_review` with the attacker-chosen URL.

6. Consequence: nothing downstream re-gates. activities.py:723-753 posts a real `post_approve_review` once the engine returns APPROVED; the engine itself has no author-association/fork gate (grep of tools/pr-approval-agent/*.py shows author_association used only for comment filtering) and `self_driving=True` relaxes the bot-author refusal (review_pr.py:222-223) and the draft prerequisite. The reviewed head is also cloned into the sandbox that holds the installation token (activities.py:431-473) — the exact fork hazard tasks.py:222-224 says fork PRs are "dropped here for security, not just cost".
verdicts.notes: Finding's code claims hold; only its line citations for the tasks facade are off (set_task_run_output is api.py:2139-2160, not 2203-2226/5768) and its framing of task_run_id/signal_report_id as attacker-supplied is wrong (it self-corrects). The real defect — missing bot-author + repo-native + PR→run linkage verification before stamping `inbox_review` — is confirmed, contradicts the code's and AGENTS.md's own stated invariant, and is reachable by any team member with task:write because signals tasks are team-controllable. Fix is two cheap checks on the already-fetched `pr` dict plus a `find_signal_implementation_run` match, mirroring `_inbox_rereview_carve_out`. Blast radius stays within the tenant (repo config is `for_team`-scoped) and an approval still requires the engine to judge the diff approvable, but the fork-code-into-sandbox exposure and the write-permission/branch-protection bypass occur regardless.

verdicts.notes: Every factual claim in the finding reproduces in the worktree. The receiver leg is the only path that stamps self-driving provenance without positively re-deriving the PR↔run linkage, bot authorship, and non-fork status — checks its sibling webhook path performs explicitly for the same feature. this_experiment_findings.problem: The initial inbox task accepts only `team_id`, `pr_url`, and `task_run_id`. It resolves the repository from `pr_url` and never verifies that the linked task run belongs to that repository. A signal task can therefore queue a Stamphog review for a PR URL that does not match the task's configured repository. This breaks the self-driving PR identity guarantee and can review an unrelated PR.
this_experiment_findings.suggestion: Load `task_run_id` through a team-scoped tasks facade and require its signal report, non-internal status, and repository to match the parsed PR repository before fetching or creating the review run. this_experiment_findings.title: Initial review does not verify self-driving provenance
this_experiment_findings.problem: The task trusts all provenance arguments from the earlier receiver. It only checks the repository config and the PR state. It does not verify `task_run_id`, `signal_report_id`, the task repository, the current reviewer toggle, bot authorship, or a repository-native head. It then marks the run as an inbox review. This mark bypasses the normal draft, bot, review-mode, and author-permission gates. A wrong or stale `TaskRun.output.pr_url` can therefore cause a real approval on a PR that is not a self-driving Inbox PR.
this_experiment_findings.suggestion: Load the exact task run through a team-scoped tasks facade before creating the review. Verify its signal report, repository, and recorded PR URL against the fetched PR. Also verify that the fetched PR is bot-authored and has a repository-native head. Resolve the acting reviewer and their current toggle again. Return without creating a run if any check fails.
